entries.proposition: System: male Long-Evans rats (81) with hippocampal electrical kindling and an implanted oxygen optode; the readout is hippocampal pO2. No WWOX, no human data, and oxygen is measured, not given.
entries.snippet: Male Hooded Long-Evans rats (N = 81; 250–300 g at the time of surgery; Charles River, Canada)

entries.proposition: Hypoxia threshold: severe hypoxia is quantified as area under 10 mmHg tissue pO2, a threshold taken from earlier work.
entries.snippet: Severe hypoxic profiles were quantified by integrating duration and depth of oxygen levels below the critical threshold (10 mmHg)

entries.proposition: Core result: repeated seizures produced postictal hypoxia that grew with each seizure in vehicle rats and did not in rats given acetaminophen or nifedipine.
entries.snippet: Vehicle-treated rats showed a progressive increase in PIH severity over time

entries.proposition: The hypoxia is prevented by blocking the vasoconstriction (cyclooxygenase, L-type calcium channels), not by supplying oxygen; no oxygen-supplementation arm exists.
entries.snippet: We adopted acetaminophen and nifedipine as experimental tools to dissociate the contribution of PIH from the contribution of the seizure itself.

entries.proposition: Seizure progression was unaffected by blocking hypoxia, so hypoxia is not shown to drive epileptogenesis.
entries.snippet: While the severity of PIH increases because of repeated seizures, repeated PIH does not contribute to kindling progression.

entries.proposition: Interictal baseline pO2 fell with repeated seizures and recovered about six days after the final seizure.
entries.snippet: rats that exhibited seizures had significantly lower interictal oxygen levels at the end of kindling that recovered back to baseline by 6 days from the final seizure

entries.proposition: Memory: seizure-exposed vehicle rats failed the novel object/context task; both drugs prevented it; PIH severity correlated negatively with performance (R2 0.35).
entries.snippet: indicating a poorer performance of rats that had more severe hypoxia

entries.proposition: Mitochondrial result: isolated hippocampal mitochondria showed lower calcium retention and lower basal and ATP-linked respiration after seizures; the respiration deficit recovered by two weeks. Only seizure-exposed hypoxic rats were compared with no-seizure controls, with n = 5.
entries.snippet: In addition, we found significantly lower basal respiration in mitochondria isolated from seizure exposed hypoxic rats compared to control rats

entries.proposition: Timing inconsistency: the Discussion says the deficit was seen 3 days after the last seizure, whereas Results test at 24 hours and 2 weeks.
entries.snippet: we still observed seizure-induced deficits in performance 3 days after their last seizure

entries.proposition: Mechanism offered is hypothesis: low mitochondrial metabolism leaves the chain reduced and favours ROS; the paper says clinical interictal hypoperfusion should be tested.
entries.snippet: It would be clinically relevant to determine if people with epilepsy have a chronically, but subtly hypoperfused seizure onset zones compared to seizure-free regions.

entries.proposition: No limitations section; the sample sizes vary by figure (n 7 to 8 for oxygen traces, n 9 for Figure 4, n 4 to 9 for behaviour, n 5 for mitochondria).
entries.snippet: Data are shown as mean ± SEM (n = 9 each group), followed by two-way repeated measure ANOVA and Sidak’s post hoc test

entries.proposition: Figures 1 to 6 opened: Fig 1 oxygen traces and area-below-10-mmHg bars (vehicle rises to about 400 mmHg min, drug groups near 0); Fig 2 group comparison; Fig 3 seizure duration and Racine stage unchanged by treatment; Fig 4 interictal pO2 about 27 to 19 mmHg in vehicle versus about 30 in drug groups, and 2-week recovery; Fig 5 discrimination index and regression; Fig 6 calcium threshold and OCR bars.
